channels.title: Konrad Fischer's Woodfire
channels.description:
My name is Konrad Fischer. I have heated my house with wood for forty years in the Black Forest, and my father did the same before me.

In Germany we do not treat wood heat as a hobby. Firewood is seasoned two years, not one. A chimney sweep inspects every stove by law. Nobody burns wet wood, because everyone was taught what wet wood does to a flue.

Most people I meet who burn wood are doing three or four things wrong that nobody ever corrected. Not because they are careless — because nobody told them. That is what this channel is for.

Every week: which woods to burn and which to never put in a stove, how to season firewood properly, how to run a stove so it holds heat all night, and how to keep a chimney safe.

Everything here comes from forty years of doing it, not from a manual.

channels.title: Gene Halvorsen
channels.description:
My name's Gene Halvorsen. I live in North Pole, Alaska, fifteen miles outside Fairbanks, where it hits forty below most winters. I hauled heating oil on the same route for thirty-seven winters and looked after houses for people who left when the cold came. I've been inside a thousand cold houses, and most of them weren't cold. They were windy.

This channel is the cheap fix first. Door sweeps, gaskets, rope caulk, a flashlight walk after dark. Fifteen dollars before five thousand. Every method has a price on it and a house where it mattered.

The book is A Thousand Cold Houses, twenty-five methods, one per chapter, at genehalvorsen.com. New video every couple of days.

channels.title: Earl Sizemore
channels.description:
I'm Earl Sizemore, up on Clinch Mountain in Hancock County, Tennessee. My daddy was the blacksmith for our end of the county, and I grew up in his shop before I could see over the anvil.

Nothing he knew was ever written down. He taught with his hands and one short sentence: do it right once and it holds.

On this channel I pass it on. How to heat a house on half the wood, stay warm and fed when the power's out for two weeks, keep the pipes from freezing, fix what breaks without calling a man, keep the mice out and the house safe. Plain talk, no fear, no gear to sell you. Just what seventy-some winters on this mountain taught me.

If a trick don't work, I'll tell you. If it can hurt you, I'll tell you twice.

My cousin Billy Ray and his wife Loretta Jean have channels of their own. Between the three of us we wrote it all down: thehillbillyway.com

Go look after your things, and after each other.
